The tools the `ai-task-tracking` MCP server lists to agents, as `tools/list` sends them: the title, the hints, the
description and the arguments. Agents call them as `mcp__ai-task-tracking__<name>`.

| Tool | Title | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| [`whats_next`](#whats_next) | What to work on next | read |
| [`get_issue`](#get_issue) | Get issue | read |
| [`get_tree`](#get_tree) | Get issue tree | read |
| [`search`](#search) | Search issues | read |
| [`list_issues`](#list_issues) | List issues | read |
| [`list_comments`](#list_comments) | List comments | read |
| [`save_issue`](#save_issue) | Save issue | write |
| [`save_issues`](#save_issues) | Save issues (batch) | write |
| [`save_comment`](#save_comment) | Add comment | write |
| [`toggle_task`](#toggle_task) | Tick checklist item | write |
| [`set_plan`](#set_plan) | Put issue in Now | write |
| [`list_projects`](#list_projects) | List projects | read |
| [`get_project`](#get_project) | Get project | read |
| [`save_project`](#save_project) | Save project | write |
| [`list_milestones`](#list_milestones) | List milestones | read |
| [`save_milestone`](#save_milestone) | Save milestone | write |
| [`get_document`](#get_document) | Get document | read |
| [`save_document`](#save_document) | Save document | write |
| [`list_issue_statuses`](#list_issue_statuses) | List statuses | read |
| [`list_issue_labels`](#list_issue_labels) | List labels | read |
| [`save_issue_label`](#save_issue_label) | Save label | write |
| [`list_teams`](#list_teams) | List ID prefixes (teams) | read |

## whats_next

**What to work on next** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

What to work on, in buckets: needsYou (waiting on the user), inProgress, readyNext (unblocked, by priority) and blocked (with blocker ids). Stalled issues carry stalled (why), failing PR checks ci (why); stalled lists your workspace's. Use it at the start of a session when no issue is named.

No arguments.

## get_issue

**Get issue** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

One issue in full (In Progress ones lead with handoff: where the last session stopped): description, links (PRs with ci: state, checks, failing), children, blockers, ancestors, the last 30 activity entries (list_comments has all), attempts (agent sessions so far) and stalled (why) if it stalled. For an epic's whole subtree use get_tree. Example: get_issue({ id: "ENG-27" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Issue id, e.g. "ENG-27". |

## get_tree

**Get issue tree** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

An issue and all its descendants with status, blockers and done/total progress; use it to check an epic. Example: get_tree({ id: "ENG-10" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Issue id, e.g. "ENG-27". |

## search

**Search issues** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

Find issues by words in title, description and comments, closed ones included. Every word must match (prefixes count), so use 1-3 distinctive words. Search before creating an issue so you don't duplicate one. Example: search({ query: "login timeout" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Words to find. |
| `limit` | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 250) |  | Max results, 1-250 (default 20). |

## list_issues

**List issues** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

Issues matching filters, most recently updated first. Open issues only unless state names a closed status or includeArchived is true. To find by words use search. Example: list_issues({ project: "Website", state: "In Progress" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string |  | Status name, case-insensitive. |
| `project` | string |  | Project name or slug. |
| `label` | string |  | Label name; bare names match group labels. |
| `parentId` | string |  | Only children of this issue id. |
| `query` | string |  | Words to match in title, description and comments. |
| `updatedAt` | string |  | Updated after this ISO date/time, or within a duration like "-P7D". |
| `limit` | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 250) |  | Page size, 1-250 (default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |
| `includeArchived` | boolean |  | Include Done, Canceled and Duplicate issues. |

## list_comments

**List comments** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

All of an issue's comments and activity, oldest first (get_issue shows only the last 30). Example: list_comments({ issueId: "ENG-27" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issueId` | string | yes | Issue id, e.g. "ENG-27". |

## save_issue

**Save issue** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`

Create or update one issue. Create: title and labels (project defaults to your repo's). Update: id and only the fields to change. For several issues at once (an epic and its steps) use save_issues. Example: save_issue({ id: "ENG-27", state: "Done", comment: "Shipped in PR #12" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  | Issue to update, e.g. "ENG-27"; omit to create. |
| `title` | string |  | Required to create. |
| `description` | string |  | Markdown; replaces the whole description. |
| `state` | string |  | Status name, e.g. Todo, In Progress, Waiting, Done, Canceled (see list_issue_statuses). Done, Canceled, Duplicate and Waiting need comment. |
| `priority` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 4) |  | 0 none, 1 urgent, 2 high, 3 medium, 4 low. |
| `project` | string |  | Project name or slug; on create, defaults to your repo's project. |
| `parentId` | string \| null |  | Parent issue id; null removes it. In save_issues also "ref:&lt;ref&gt;". |
| `milestone` | string \| null |  | Milestone name in the project; null clears it. |
| `labels` | string[] |  | Replaces all labels; creating needs one. Bare names match group labels ("Web" = "Scope/Web"); new names are created. |
| `addLabels` | string[] |  | Labels to add. |
| `removeLabels` | string[] |  | Labels to remove. |
| `blockedBy` | string[] |  | Ids of blocking issues; replaces the list ([] clears). In save_issues also "ref:&lt;ref&gt;". |
| `addBlockedBy` | string[] |  | Blocker ids to add. |
| `removeBlockedBy` | string[] |  | Blocker ids to remove. |
| `relatedTo` | string[] |  | Related issue ids; replaces the list (set on both issues). |
| `addRelatedTo` | string[] |  | Related ids to add. |
| `removeRelatedTo` | string[] |  | Related ids to remove. |
| `dueDate` | string \| null |  | YYYY-MM-DD; null clears it. |
| `links` | { url, title? }[] |  | Links to add: [{ url, title }]. |
| `removeLinks` | string[] |  | Link URLs to remove. |
| `baseDescription` | string |  | The text you edited from; the save is refused if it changed since. |
| `comment` | string |  | Comment saved with the change. Required for Done, Canceled, Duplicate, Waiting: what shipped or what it waits on. GitHub PR/commit URLs in it become issue links. |

## save_issues

**Save issues (batch)** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`

Create or update several issues in one call; every item is checked before any is written. Use it for an epic and its steps. Example: save_issues({ issues: [{ ref: "epic", title: "Epic: import", labels: ["Feature"] }, { ref: "s1", parentId: "ref:epic", title: "Step 1: parse", labels: ["Task"] }, { parentId: "ref:epic", title: "Step 2: load", labels: ["Task"], blockedBy: ["ref:s1"] }] })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issues` | object[] (at least 1) | yes | Items in order. Each takes the save_issue arguments (same names and meanings) plus ref. |

## save_comment

**Add comment** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`

Add a comment to an issue: findings, decisions, PR links (GitHub PR/commit URLs are also added to its links). When you also change the status, pass comment to save_issue instead. Example: save_comment({ issueId: "ENG-27", body: "Root cause: stale cache." })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issueId` | string | yes | Issue id, e.g. "ENG-27". |
| `body` | string | yes | Markdown text. |

## toggle_task

**Tick checklist item** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`

Tick or untick one "- [ ]" checklist item in an issue description without rewriting it. Example: toggle_task({ id: "ENG-42", index: 0, line: "- [ ] Write the migration" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Issue id, e.g. "ENG-27". |
| `index` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 9007199254740991) | yes | Position among the description's checklist lines, from 0 (code blocks skipped). |
| `line` | string | yes | The item's current line; refused if it no longer matches. |

## set_plan

**Put issue in Now** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

Put an issue in the user's Now slot. Agents may only set "now" (moving to In Progress does it too); Next and Later belong to the user. Example: set_plan({ id: "ENG-27", plan: "now" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Issue id, e.g. "ENG-27". |
| `plan` | "now" \| "next" \| "later" \| null | yes | "now". (next, later and null are for the user.) |

## list_projects

**List projects** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

All projects with their issue-id key, status and open/total issue counts.

No arguments.

## get_project

**Get project** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

One project: description, milestones with progress, document ids and mapped repos. Example: get_project({ query: "Website" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Project name or slug. |

## save_project

**Save project** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`

Create a project (name), or update one (id). Its issue-id key comes from the name at creation and never changes. Example: save_project({ name: "Website", description: "Marketing site" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  | Slug of the project to update; omit to create. |
| `name` | string |  | Required to create; on update it renames. |
| `description` | string |  | Markdown; replaces the current description. |
| `state` | string |  | Project status, e.g. Planned, Active, Completed. |
| `baseDescription` | string |  | The text you edited from; the save is refused if it changed since. |

## list_milestones

**List milestones** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

A project's milestones with target dates and progress. Example: list_milestones({ project: "Website" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | yes | Project name or slug. |

## save_milestone

**Save milestone** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

Create a milestone in a project, or update the one with that name. Only for a release or date the user named; assign issues with save_issue's milestone. Example: save_milestone({ project: "Website", name: "Beta", targetDate: "2027-02-01" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | yes | Project name or slug. |
| `name` | string | yes | Milestone name; matches an existing one case-insensitively. |
| `description` | string |  | Markdown. |
| `targetDate` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD. |

## get_document

**Get document** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

A project document by id or exact title (get_project lists a project's documents). Example: get_document({ id: "website/architecture" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Document id "&lt;project&gt;/&lt;doc&gt;", or its title. |

## save_document

**Save document** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`

Create a markdown document in a project, or replace one by id. Example: save_document({ project: "Website", title: "Architecture", content: "# Overview" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | yes | Project name or slug. |
| `title` | string | yes | Document title. |
| `content` | string | yes | Markdown; replaces the whole document. |
| `id` | string |  | Document id "&lt;project&gt;/&lt;doc&gt;" to replace; omit to create. |
| `baseContent` | string |  | The text you edited from; the save is refused if it changed since. |

## list_issue_statuses

**List statuses** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

The statuses save_issue's state accepts, with their type (backlog, unstarted, started, completed, canceled, duplicate).

No arguments.

## list_issue_labels

**List labels** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

All labels; grouped ones have full names like "Scope/Web".

No arguments.

## save_issue_label

**Save label** · write · hints: `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

Create a label in a group, or change a label's color. save_issue creates plain labels on the fly, so use this only for groups or colors. Example: save_issue_label({ name: "Web", parent: "Scope" })

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Label name, or the full "Group/Name". |
| `color` | string |  | Hex color, e.g. "#4ea7fc". |
| `parent` | string |  | Group name; the label becomes "&lt;parent&gt;/&lt;name&gt;". |

## list_teams

**List ID prefixes (teams)** · read-only · hints: `readOnlyHint`, `openWorldHint: false`

Issue-id keys (e.g. "ENG") and the projects using each. Projects are the main unit; prefer list_projects.

No arguments.
